Hi Raina,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — it was great to see the TheraHealth use case.

As promised, a short recap focused on what gets stored from user queries (prompts) and model outputs, and where/how long by default. See the attached "data_capture_matrix_v1.pdf" with a compact matrix.

High-level summary:
- Default behavior (hosted): prompts and responses are treated as transient telemetry. We do NOT persist raw prompt text or model outputs unless customers enable one of the explicit persistence options below.
- Session recording: if you enable "session recording" on a workspace, raw prompts + responses are persisted encrypted in your chosen region for up to 90 days (configurable 30–365 days).
- Output persistence: customers can enable "persist_outputs" per route; when enabled, generated outputs are stored for 30 days by default and can be configured 0–365 days.
- KV / inference cache: kept in-memory and on-disk cache shards per instance; caches are ephemeral and pruned after 4 hours of inactivity by default (configurable).
- Audit logs & telemetry (request metadata, timestamps, model version): retained separately for 365 days for SLA/compliance purposes.

Encryption & keys:
- Data at rest is encrypted with service-managed keys by default. Customers may bring their own KMS keys (BYOK) for Private and Dedicated deployments.
- In-transit TLS is always enforced.

Region & residency:
- For hosted customers you can choose region (us/eu) when provisioning the workspace; recorded or persisted items are stored only in the selected region.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether you need per-environment (prod/staging) retention settings.
2) Let me know if TheraHealth requires BYOK or an on-prem snapshot for audit.
3) Any immediate SOC2 artifacts we should share — I can attach our summary and open a redaction-friendly export for you.

If the matrix attached is sufficient, we can include these details in the mutual action plan and Marcus will scope any needed custom retention settings.

Best,

Hi Raina — quick answers inline to keep this actionable.

- Per-environment retention: Yes. Workspaces support environment-scoped retention policies. You can set different TTLs for "persist_outputs" and "session_recording" on prod vs staging. We can set prod persist_outputs = 90 days, staging = 0 (ephemeral) as part of the onboarding configuration.

- Redaction/tokenization: Redwood does not automatically perform semantic redaction of PII before persisting outputs today. Two options we recommend:
  1) Client-side redaction: post-process inputs/outputs in your app prior to sending to Redwood (we provide libraries and examples).
  2) Server-side hooks: we can run a pre-persist filter (Lambda-style webhook) that inspects and redacts tokens before storage; this is available for Dedicated and Private customers and can be scoped for Hosted with an enterprise add-on.

- Region/residency: EU (eu-west-1) is available for hosted workspaces. When you select the EU workspace, recorded/persisted content and audit logs are stored in eu-west-1. Cross-region backups are optional and explicit (we won't replicate without customer consent).

- KMS/BYOK: Supported on Dedicated/Private and on hosted via enterprise BYOK for encrypting persisted artifacts.

I've attached an updated capture matrix and a short SOC2 evidence pack link. If TheraHealth needs PII tokenization as a managed service we can include a scope item in the SOW.

Next steps:
- Naomi: send over the mutual action plan with prod/staging retention values and a call to confirm BYOK need.
- Raina: tell us whether you want us to enable persist_outputs for prod (90 days) and keep staging disabled; also indicate whether you want eu-west-1.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.
